hypothesis: For every registered cell, the total variation distance between the backend's empirical distribution over [CC, CD, DC, DD] and the protocol's exact Born distribution is at most tvdThreshold.
falsifiedIf: Any single registered cell exceeds tvdThreshold. Not a majority, not an average — an average over cells would let a clean cell pay for a broken one.
claimBoundary: This tests whether the device reproduces the predicted distributions. It is NOT a test of quantum advantage, of any equilibrium, or of human behaviour, and release 1 claims none of those.
backendSelection: pinned; least_busy is not used, so every cell runs on the same device
statistic: total variation distance, 0.5 * sum |empirical - exact| over the four profiles

thresholdBasis.method: Aer noise-model prediction, computed and committed BEFORE registration
thresholdBasis.why_not_calibrated: No IBM token was configured when the threshold was derived, so a generic superconducting model stands in. Generic and stated is honest; a threshold tuned to the device after seeing its calibration would not be.
thresholdBasis.threshold_rule: min(0.25, 2 * worst predicted TVD + 0.05). Doubling absorbs the gap between a generic model and a real device; the cap keeps a pathological prediction from setting a threshold nothing could fail.

readoutMitigation: Raw counts only. Mitigated figures, if computed, are published as a separate record and never substituted for these.
commitment: Every registered cell will be executed at or after drawAfter on the named backend, and every cell's raw counts published whatever they say — not the cells that came out well. If the backend is unavailable the run is abandoned and reported as abandoned; it is not silently re-pointed at another device, and simulator output is never published here.
